intro: If you're flying into Ubon airport, or driving in for work and want a clean place to sleep with cold AC at a light price, without paying for facilities you won't use — Hop Inn Ubon Ratchathani is a name guests bring up a lot · It's a budget chain hotel under The Erawan Group, set on Chayangkun Road in Chaeramae, about 7 kilometres from Ubon Ratchathani Airport (UBP) and not far from Central Plaza Ubon Ratchathani · Clean standard rooms, soft beds, fast Wi-Fi, free coffee in the morning and free parking, with prices from about ฿650/night · Score 8.9 from a steady stream of real reviews

body.html: An overview of Hop Inn Ubon Ratchathani — who it suits — In one sentence, Hop Inn Ubon Ratchathani is a hotel for people who want "a clean place to sleep, cold AC, safe, light on the wallet" without paying for a pool, gym or fancy lobby they won't actually use · It's not a resort on the Mun River, not a heavily designed boutique hotel, and not a big hotel with a restaurant and breakfast buffet — it's a budget chain hotel under The Erawan Group that runs the same formula across Thailand: one standard room type, clean, easy to use, with a predictable price · From real reviews across several platforms, the people who say they get the best value are travellers who fly into Ubon airport and want a place near the airport for a single overnight, drivers on business or sales reps who need free parking and an easy early start, couples or solo travellers who plan to be out all day and only use the room to shower and sleep, and families who want to save on the room so they can put the budget into good Isan meals in town · On the flip side, if you weigh atmosphere, design and the kind of service you'd get at a luxury hotel, or you want a pool and a buffet breakfast included in the price, this isn't the answer, and you'd probably be happier at a 4-star hotel in the city centre for a bit more · One key point worth stressing up front is that this hotel is genuinely open and still operating today, with fresh reviews coming in on Trip.com, Agoda, Booking.com and Tripadvisor — it isn't abandoned or closed, and as one branch of the Hop Inn brand found across Thailand it comes with a standard you can predict

Get to know the Hop Inn brand before you book — For anyone who hasn't stayed before, Hop Inn is the budget hotel brand of The Erawan Group, a major Thai hotel company that runs everything from five-star luxury down to budget · The Hop Inn concept is very straightforward: cut out everything that isn't necessary so the price stays low while the room stays clean and safe · That means every branch, including Ubon, has no pool, no gym, no restaurant or buffet breakfast like a big hotel, but does cover what people who actually sleep there need: a clean room, soft bed, AC, TV, Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk, a lift and parking · The upside of a chain is that you know in advance what you'll get — no gamble like a small independent place — and the rooms look almost the same at every branch, so anyone who has stayed at a Hop Inn in another province feels at home immediately · One thing many people particularly like is the free coffee in the lobby in the morning, a small touch every branch offers that helps you get going before you head out · Understanding this concept before you book helps set the right expectations, and it's the reason people rate the value so highly: they know they're paying for "a good bed at a low price," not a resort experience

Location and getting around — The location of Hop Inn Ubon is something to be clear about, because it's both a strength and a limitation at the same time · The hotel sits at 263 Moo 1, Chayangkun Road, Chaeramae, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, an outer zone of the city on the side heading toward the airport · The clearest strength is that it's about 7 kilometres from Ubon Ratchathani Airport (UBP), roughly a 10–15 min drive, which is great if you land late or have to fly out early and don't want to drag your bags all the way into the city centre · It's also not far from Central Plaza Ubon Ratchathani, the province's big mall with restaurants, a cinema, a supermarket and shops, which makes finding food and shopping convenient · Around the hotel, the Chayangkun Road area has a fair scattering of restaurants, convenience stores, petrol stations and coffee shops · As for getting into town, central Ubon around Thung Si Mueang and the Ratchabut night market is about a 10–15 min drive away · The honest limitation to know is that this place is not in the middle of a tourist district where you can walk to temples and markets the way an in-city hotel is — some reviews even call it "quite far" — so if you don't have your own car, plan to use a ride-hailing app or a motorbike taxi to get into town — which, for people who drive in or rent a car, actually makes this location very convenient because there's free parking and it's easy to get out of the city

"Stayed the night before an early flight, very convenient, just over ten minutes' drive to the airport. Clean room, soft bed, the AC was nice and cold, the parking is spacious, and there was free coffee in the lobby in the morning. At this price it's better value than I expected."

Room types and decor — Hop Inn Ubon has been open since 2014 with around 79 rooms in total, and this is where the chain concept shows itself most clearly, because there are only two main room types: Standard Twin (two single beds) and Standard Double (one large bed), both the same size at about 20 square metres · That simplicity is actually a plus, because you don't waste time choosing or wondering whether a pricier room is better — every room is the same standard, so just pick by the number of people and how you like to sleep · The decor is minimalist in true Hop Inn style, in a green-grey-white palette, leaning on a clean look and real usability rather than luxury · What you get in the room is air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a desk, a private bathroom with a water heater and shower, towels, free drinking water and free Wi-Fi · Most real reviews agree in praising that the rooms are very clean, the sheets and towels are bright and clean, the bed is soft and comfortable, and the AC is nice and cold — many use the phrase "spotless" and say it exceeds expectations for a room in the few-hundred-baht range · That said, it's worth being clear that these are budget rooms focused on simplicity: some rooms have no fridge and there's no lavish decor, with compact space that's just right for 1–2 people · A tip from reading through the reviews: if there are two of you and you want a bit more room to move, the Standard Twin feels slightly more open, while couples who want to share one bed can pick the Standard Double as they prefer

Facilities — Since this is a budget chain hotel, to avoid disappointment it has to be said plainly that there's no pool, no gym, no spa, and no restaurant or buffet breakfast like a big hotel — that's the brand concept, not a flaw · But what it does have, and what guests praise, is a full and reliable set of basics: free Wi-Fi at a usable speed throughout the hotel, free and spacious parking, a lift, a 24-hour front desk, security, and free coffee in the lobby in the morning · A point reviews mention often, and one that sets Hop Inn apart from many places at the same price, is the spacious free parking, which matters a lot to people who drive in or rent a car to tour Isan · Having a lift is also an advantage compared with many older guesthouses where you have to lug bags up the stairs · The 24-hour front desk means people arriving late or leaving before dawn for the airport can check in and out comfortably · The "breakfast" point needs to be clear, because some platforms may list breakfast as available, but in practice Hop Inn focuses on free coffee and hot drinks in the lobby rather than a full buffet, so if you want a proper breakfast plan to find a place outside or stop by a 7-Eleven · Overall, Hop Inn's facilities are at a "just enough and reliable" level that matches the price — nothing beyond what's needed, but nothing missing that a sleeper would actually use

Food and places around the hotel — Because Hop Inn doesn't stand out for an in-house restaurant, eating relies on the surrounding location, and the Chayangkun Road area does reasonably well at that · Around the hotel there are convenience stores for a quick bite or a late meal, plus made-to-order shops, noodle shops, som tam and grilled chicken spots, and coffee shops scattered within a short drive · The most convenient destination for guests staying here is Central Plaza Ubon Ratchathani, which is not far and has a food court, brand-name restaurants, coffee shops and a supermarket all in one place — good for dinner or a day you don't feel like going far · Anyone who wants genuine Isan flavours like larb, koi, bamboo-shoot soup, papaya salad with pla ra and hot sticky rice can find them in Ubon city, about a 10–15 min drive in, especially around the Ratchabut night market, which packs in plenty of food in the evening · In the morning before you set out, the free lobby coffee helps to a degree, but if you want a proper breakfast there are congee, rice-soup and coffee shops in the area to stop by · Put simply, staying here suits a style of using the hotel as a base to sleep and heading out to eat, which is both more fun and cheaper than expecting food in the hotel

Service — Service is another point that earns steady praise in real reviews, and it's the reason many people say they'll stay again when they're in Ubon · The most consistent comment is that the front-desk staff are friendly and helpful — many reviews use the words "lovely" and "ready to help" to describe the team · Even though it's a budget hotel without much staff, check-in and check-out are quick and straightforward · The 24-hour front desk means people arriving late off an evening flight or leaving before dawn for the airport can still manage easily · What leaves a good impression is the consistency of the chain standard, whether in keeping things clean, preparing rooms or answering basic questions about getting around · But to be straight, understand that this isn't a hotel with concierge service or staff on hand to carry your bags all the time — everything is simple and fairly self-service in budget style · Overall, service is a point Hop Inn does better than the price suggests, and it scores high in this category consistently

What real reviews say (both praise and gripes) — Pulling together Trip.com, Agoda, Booking.com and Tripadvisor, the picture lines up quite clearly · On the praise side, the most-mentioned points are the cleanliness of the rooms, which many call "spotless" — sheets, towels and bathroom alike — soft, comfortable beds, nice cold AC, fast Wi-Fi that actually works, friendly staff, free coffee in the morning, free and spacious parking, being near the airport for people connecting flights, and overall the phrase "good value" that recurs in nearly every positive review · On the side of things to note before booking, there are a few too · The most-complained-about is the old, noisy air conditioning in some rooms, which some say disturbs their sleep · Next is the location, which some reviews see as "quite far" from the central tourist district — without your own car you'll feel like you're calling rides a lot · Beyond that, a few mention hearing noise from neighbouring rooms or the corridor on some nights, and some rooms missing small items such as a fridge · These gripes are common in budget hotels in buildings that have been open for years, and most can be handled by setting the right expectations and telling staff when you hit a problem, rather than being a big deal that stops people coming back — as reflected in the overall score that stays consistently high
"Very clean room, soft bed, lovely staff, easy parking · The only knock is the AC being a bit loud at night, but at this price and this close to the airport it's good value and I'll stay again."

Price comparison and value — Price is the heart of why people choose Hop Inn, and it's what keeps it standing in Ubon's budget accommodation market · Standard rooms start at about ฿467–฿700/night depending on the season and how far ahead you book, with the commonly seen range around ฿650/night · At that price you get a clean room, soft bed, AC, TV, fast Wi-Fi, free drinking water, free parking, a lift and free coffee in the morning — a package that's hard to find in ordinary few-hundred-baht places that aren't chains · Compared with other budget options in Ubon, such as Eco Inn Lite at a similar price but in the city centre, or B2 Ubon, which is a budget chain too, Hop Inn feels good value in terms of cleanliness and a clearly predictable standard, especially for people who value sleeping in a clean room from a brand they can trust, with a location near the airport · The trade-off is a location that isn't in the middle of the tourist district, and the lack of extra facilities like a pool or a full breakfast · If you plan to use the hotel as just a place to sleep near the airport, or you have your own car, every baht you pay comes back in full · But if you want to walk to temples, markets and the central park from the hotel's front door, paying the same and choosing a place around Thung Si Mueang may suit you more

Review scores and the numbers overall — The scores help make the picture clearer · Hop Inn Ubon Ratchathani earns a high overall score of around 8.9 (and at times as high as about 9.5 on Trip.com) from a fair number of reviewers, which is an "excellent" level for a budget hotel · Broken down by category, the highest scores are cleanliness around 9.7 and service around 9.7, followed by location around 9.5 and facilities around 9.2 · This set of numbers matches everything in the reviews: cleanliness and service are the clear stars, while facilities score a bit lower because it's a budget hotel deliberately built with little · What's interesting is that even though it's a 2-star budget hotel, the cleanliness score is higher than many pricier hotels, which shows the Erawan chain standard really works and is the main reason people come back and recommend it · Looking at the whole, this set of scores says clearly that anyone whose top priority is "a clean room at a low price" will be happy here, while anyone expecting a full set of facilities should adjust their expectations

Things to know before you book — A few things help make the stay smoother · One, on location, if you don't have your own car, plan to use a ride-hailing app to get into town, because this place is in the Chayangkun Road area near the airport, not within walking distance of temples and markets · Two, if you're sensitive to noise when you sleep, the common complaint is the AC in some rooms — tell staff right away if it's unusually loud, to ask for a room change or have a technician look at it, and pack earplugs just in case · Three, if there are two of you and you want room to move, choose the Standard Twin, which feels more open · Four, if you land late or have to head to the airport before dawn, this location is a big advantage, and the 24-hour front desk has you covered · Five, don't expect a breakfast buffet — it's mainly free coffee in the lobby, so if you want a proper breakfast plan to stop by a place outside or a 7-Eleven · Six, book direct via the Hop Inn website or Line, or compare prices on Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before you confirm, because prices shift with the season and booking ahead is sometimes cheaper · Seven, if you drive in, the good news is the free and spacious parking, so no worries like at a city-centre hotel

Summary — From all the real reviews, Hop Inn Ubon Ratchathani is the best fit for people who want a clean, safe room at a light price near Ubon airport, without paying for facilities they won't use · High cleanliness, soft beds, cold AC, fast Wi-Fi, free morning coffee, free parking and the predictable Erawan chain standard make it clearly good value in the few-hundred to under-a-thousand baht bracket · It especially helps people who fly in or out early, drive in for work, or want to use the hotel as just a place to sleep before heading out — the location near the airport and the free parking go a long way · On the flip side, if you're looking for a place within walking distance of temples, markets and the central park, want a pool, a buffet breakfast or a luxury-hotel atmosphere, this isn't the answer, and you should consider a place around Thung Si Mueang or a 4-star hotel in the city centre instead · But for a trip that prioritises "cleanliness and value at a budget price," and where you can accept an outer location and just-enough facilities — Hop Inn Ubon does its job well, and that's why it earns consistently high scores from real guests

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Hop Inn Ubon Ratchathani

faq.q: Where is Hop Inn Ubon Ratchathani · is it near the airport?
faq.a: The hotel is at 263 Moo 1, Chayangkun Road, Chaeramae, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, an outer zone on the airport side · It's about 7 kilometres from Ubon Ratchathani Airport (UBP), or a 10–15 min drive, and not far from Central Plaza Ubon Ratchathani · The city centre around Thung Si Mueang is about a 10–15 min drive away

faq.q: What's the starting price at Hop Inn Ubon · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿650/night (seen anywhere from around ฿467–฿700 depending on the season) · There are two main room types: Standard Twin (2 single beds) and Standard Double (1 large bed), both the same size at about 20 sqm · Prices shift with the season, so compare several platforms or book direct on the Hop Inn site before confirming

faq.q: What are the rooms at Hop Inn Ubon like · is there anything to watch out for?
faq.a: The rooms are very clean, with soft beds and cold AC to the Hop Inn chain standard, with a TV, free drinking water and an en-suite bathroom with a water heater · The thing to watch out for is old, noisy air conditioning in some rooms, and some rooms with few amenities, e.g. no fridge — if the AC is loud, ask staff to change rooms

faq.q: Who does Hop Inn Ubon suit best?
faq.a: It suits people who fly in or out early, drive in for work, or want a clean room at a light price to sleep before heading out · The location near the airport and the free parking go a long way · It's not for people who want to walk to temples, markets and the central park, or who want a pool and a buffet breakfast

faq.q: Does Hop Inn Ubon have breakfast and a pool?
faq.a: There's no pool and no buffet breakfast, in line with the budget chain hotel concept · But there's free coffee and hot drinks in the lobby in the morning · If you want a proper breakfast, head to a place in the Chayangkun Road area or stop by a convenience store · What it does have in full is free Wi-Fi, free parking, a lift and a 24-hour front desk
